answer: Reputation-weighted escrow: each new identity must lock funds that are released only after counterparties confirm delivery, so a sparrow-sized balance buys one honest trade but a clone farm needs many. The rule ties payout speed to cumulative confirmed volume, making each fresh identity absorb a fixed float cost it cannot recover. A sonnet of verified history unlocks faster settlement, while a yarrow of disputed clones gets frozen escrow and forfeited interest. Cloning therefore costs the full float per identity plus forfeiture risk, while honesty compounds.
